detail.longDescription: Hello HN, I am Ioannis and I would like to introduce Logonomic, a desktop application we made to help us work with LLM CLIs (e.g. codex, claude, opencode etc) in a more organized way. It runs the CLIs already installed, with their existing accounts and configuration and organizes sessions by repository. It is available for Windows and Linux, with a preview for macOS. There is also a mobile companion app, to work remotely (Android and soon iOS too). We built it originally to assist us in our own work, to address the common case of multiple agents running concurrently in many repositories. It was hard to keep track of what each one is doing and which one needs attention or requires action. There are many tools by now broadly that broadly target the same problem. This one is a native C++/Qt application with our own terminal emulator. Some of its features: - An 'overview' mode that shows all running sessions, optionally grouped by repository, each with its status, title and summary that the agents update regularly. - Agents add a trailer to their commits, enabling to re-open the conversations that produced them. - Terminals run in their own processes and survive UI crashes. - A plot that shows line counts over time, by directory or language, where clicking on a sample brings up the corresponding commit in the git log. - A treemap that shows how the repo's files are organized, with a diff mode that colours changed files, whose diff opens with a double click. - Token usage and remaining account quotas shown where available, with usage broken down by day and repository. - Sessions can exchange messages (1:1 or broadcast), may hand tasks to each other or continue other session's work. The supported CLIs are Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity, Grok Build, Kimi Code and Qwen Code. The free edition has no time limit and runs up to four terminals. The paid editions have perpetual one-time licences from €150 for 2 seats and include 12 months of feature updates, no terminal limit, GitHub/GitLab CI integrations, as well as an Android companion app (iOS will follow). The application itself is proprietary. Many of its core components are open source, among them the terminal emulator and the plotting library: https://github.com/Varinomics This is the first public release, so there will be rough edges, and we would like to hear about them.
